full_failure_r2.cause: Test-side missing barrier. The test emits the VPN drop and goes straight into five iterations of (read the failure count from the file, refreshPreflight, settle until the count grows). A preflight retries only while a repair is pending: RuntimeHostPreflight.swift:92 calls observeHelperForSplitDNS, which guards on splitDNSRepair.shouldRetry, i.e. pending != nil (RuntimeHost.swift:1182). Since 1b the drop's removal is queued on PlatformWork and recorded in a later turn, while the preflight reads the helper on a global queue and can complete first. Iteration 1 refreshed before the drop's failure was recorded (no retry is correct production behavior then), and its settle was satisfied by the drop's own failure. Iterations 2-5 each got one retry: 1 + 4 = 5. The sibling tests already settle on the drop's refusal first (:384, :431). Not a production defect; the 1b offload widened the window.

barrier.change: one line after harness.vpn.emit(.disconnected(reason: .networkLost)) and before the five refreshes: await harness.settle("the drop's removal was refused") { !self.hostEvents(harness, "platform.split_dns_failed").isEmpty }
barrier.why_causal: SplitDNSEntryFileRepair.record sets pending (:179) before it appends platform.split_dns_failed (:183), in one synchronous call, and the events writer is FIFO. So the drop's failure visible in the file means the repair is pending, and every later refresh has a repair to retry. The loop arithmetic then guarantees the count: the barrier makes before_1 >= 1, each iteration requires count > before_k, so before_{k+1} >= before_k + 1 and the count after five iterations is >= 6. An interleaved 1 s helper-check retry only adds failures.
